Why TikTok labels your photo or video “AI-generated” — and how to remove the metadata behind it

Posted a photo, a carousel or a video and TikTok tagged it “AI-generated” even though you only used AI for a small part of it? The label is often triggered by metadata inside the file. Here is how it works and how to clean it.

Updated 2026-11-07 · 5 min read

Open IA Cleaner

What is TikTok’s “AI-generated” label?

TikTok shows an “AI-generated” label on videos and photos that were created or significantly edited with AI. It can appear because you turned on the AI-generated content setting yourself, because the content was made with TikTok’s own AI effects, or because TikTok detected it automatically.

How TikTok detects it automatically

TikTok reads C2PA Content Credentials: a signed record that many AI generators and some editing apps embed in the file, saying how it was made. If the record says AI was involved, TikTok can add the label as soon as you upload.

In a video, that information lives in special boxes of the MP4 or MOV container, next to other metadata:

  • C2PA manifest — the Content Credentials themselves.
  • XMP — can include the IPTC field DigitalSourceType with values like trainedAlgorithmicMedia.
  • User data — the app or encoder that produced the video, and often the GPS location where it was recorded.

Photos and carousels

Photo posts work the same way. An image made or edited with an AI tool can carry C2PA Content Credentials and XMP fields such as DigitalSourceType, plus EXIF data like the camera, the editing app and the GPS location. If you post several images in a carousel, each one can carry its own metadata, so clean all of them — IA Cleaner lets you drop them at once and download everything in a single ZIP.

Step 1 — Check what your video contains

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Images (photos) or Video.
  2. Drop the photos (JPG, PNG, WebP) or the video (MP4, MOV) you were going to post. You can also do it from your phone’s browser.
  3. Look for entries such as C2PA / Content Credentials (uuid), XMP (uuid) or User data (udta), and for AI-related words in the report.

Step 2 — Remove the metadata and upload the clean copy

  1. Click Download clean image or Download clean video (or Download all for a carousel). Cleaning is lossless: pixels and frames are not re-encoded, so quality stays the same.
  2. Upload those files to TikTok.
  3. Clean it as the last step: if you open and export the video again in an editor, it may write the metadata back.

What this can’t guarantee

  • Metadata is one of the signals. Content made with TikTok’s own AI effects is labeled by TikTok itself, TikTok has its own detection, and it has announced invisible watermarks for AI content made with its tools. Removing metadata doesn’t affect any of that.
  • TikTok’s rules ask you to label realistic content that was generated or significantly edited with AI, and unlabeled content can be labeled, limited or removed. If your video is AI-generated, label it — this tool is for files whose metadata doesn’t reflect what you actually did, and for removing private data like your location.
